assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air has no color and no smell at all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that air has no color and no smell, which is a property of gases but not the specific property of shape and volume that G5-M-3 requires. It does not address definite/indefinite shape or volume, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Air has no color and no smell at all, which is why we cannot see it!
copy.tl: Walang kulay at walang amoy ang hangin, kaya nga hindi natin ito nakikita!
copy.bis: Walay kolor ug walay baho ang hangin, mao nga dili nato kini makita!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the air pressure inside gets stronger than the rubber can handle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes air pressure causing the rubber to tear and burst, not how forces change an object's shape (pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, squeezed). It shares the idea of force/pressure on an object but does not directly teach shape change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the rubber can handle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rubber's limit but does not describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It is about bursting from pressure, not identifying or describing material properties.

copy.en: Keep blowing up a balloon, and the air pressure inside gets stronger than the rubber can handle. Then—POP! The rubber tears and the balloon bursts!
copy.tl: Patuloy mong punuin ng hangin ang balloon, at ang air pressure sa loob ay lalakas kaysa sa kaya ng goma. Pagkatapos—POP! Mapuputol ang goma at puputok ang balloon!
copy.bis: Padayon nimo pun-on og hangin ang balloon, ug ang air pressure sa sulod molakas unta kay sa kaya sa goma. Dayon—POP! Maputol ang goma ug moputok ang balloon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they can sneak deep into our lungs and cause health problems
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs and health problems but does not identify parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work. It only references lungs in the context of PM2.5 harm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PM2.5 are tiny air particles less than 2.5 micrometres wide
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses air particles but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It does not teach the composition of air.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they can sneak deep into our lungs and cause health problems
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a health problem from air pollution but does not describe possible effects of human activities on living things in an ecosystem. It lacks the ecosystem context and the link to human activities like deforestation or pollution as a broad environmental issue.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PM2.5 are tiny air particles less than 2.5 micrometres wide
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a type of air pollutant but does not identify local community issues/concerns or how science could address them, such as waste treatment. It does not connect to community-level problem-solving.

copy.en: PM2.5 are tiny air particles less than 2.5 micrometres wide! They are too small to see, but they can sneak deep into our lungs and cause health problems.
copy.tl: Ang PM2.5 ay napakaliit na particle sa hangin na wala pang 2.5 micrometers! Masyado silang maliit para makita, pero pwede silang pumasok nang malalim sa baga at magdulot ng sakit.
copy.bis: Ang PM2.5 mga napaka-gagmayng particle sa hangin nga ubos sa 2.5 micrometro! Gamay kaayo sila aron makita, apan makalusot sa lawom sa baga ug magdulot og mga problema sa kalusugan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A comfortable 24-25°C is kinder to your body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature in degrees Celsius and a thermostat, but it does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It only discusses a comfortable aircon setting, which is not instructional support for the heat vs. temperature concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A comfortable 24-25°C is kinder to your body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the unit degrees Celsius but does not identify or teach how to appropriately use units in science activities. It merely states a temperature value in a comfort context, providing no direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
Is the lowest aircon setting always the best?

Nope! A comfortable 24-25°C is kinder to your body. It keeps you from getting too chilly and avoids colds. The thermostat helps keep it just right!
copy.tl:
Laging mas maganda ba ang pinakamababang setting ng aircon?

Hindi! Ang komportableng 24-25°C ay mas mabuti sa katawan. Iwas ka sa sobrang lamig at sipon. Ang thermostat ang tumutulong panatilihin ang tamang temperatura!
copy.bis:
Kanunay ba mas maayo ang pinakaubos nga setting sa aircon?

Dili! Ang komportableng 24-25°C mas maayo sa lawas. Makalikay ka sa sobra ka-tugnaw ug sip-on. Ang thermostat motabang sa pagpabilin sa hustong temperatura!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your refrigerator uses a thermostat too!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a household appliance and temperature-related operation, but it does not identify sources or uses of light, sound, or heat energy. The thermostat's function is about temperature control, not about heat energy sources or uses.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When it's cold enough inside, it shuts off the motor.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to cold and warm conditions but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It only describes a thermostat's on/off behavior, which is not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: Your refrigerator uses a thermostat too! When it's cold enough inside, it shuts off the motor. When you open the door and it warms up, it hums again!
copy.tl: Gumagamit din ng thermostat ang ref ninyo! Kapag malamig na ang loob, pinapatay nito ang motor. Pag binuksan mo at uminit, uugong ulit ito!
copy.bis: Naggamit pod og thermostat ang inyong ref! Kon bugnaw na ang sulod, palungon niini ang motor. Pag ablihan nimo ug mo-init, mo-ugong ulit kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An air conditioner has a thermostat that measures temperature and automatically stops cooling when the room is cool enough!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature measurement by a thermostat but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It provides no comparison or conceptual instruction on heat vs. temperature, so it only shares the vocabulary 'temperature' without supporting the competency.

copy.en: An air conditioner has a thermostat that measures temperature and automatically stops cooling when the room is cool enough!
copy.tl: May thermostat ang aircon na sumusukat ng temperatura at awtomatikong pinapatay ang paglamig kapag sapat na ang lamig!
copy.bis: Adunay thermostat ang aircon nga magsukod sa temperatura ug awtomatik nga mohunong sa pagpabugnaw kon bugnaw na ang kwarto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: He helped break the secret Enigma code during World War II
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Alan Turing as a famous foreign scientist, but it describes his code-breaking achievement, not an invention. The competency specifically requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s, so the card does not directly support the skill.

copy.en:
What secret code did Alan Turing help break?

He helped break the secret Enigma code during World War II, which was super hard!
copy.tl:
Anong sikretong code ang tinulungan bumasag ni Alan Turing?

Tumulong siyang bumasag ng sikretong Enigma code noong World War II na sobrang hirap!
copy.bis:
Unang sekretong code ang gitabangan bungkagon ni Alan Turing?

Mitabang siya sa pagbungkag sa sekretong Enigma code panahon sa World War II nga lisod kaayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some tiny microalgae can store lots of oil in their cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions microalgae and their cells, but does not teach the distinction between unicellular and multicellular organisms. It does not state that microalgae are single-celled or contrast them with multicellular organisms, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists are studying algae as a renewable biofuel to replace fossil fuels
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about algae as a biofuel source, which relates to energy but not to light, sound, or heat energy sources and uses. It does not address any of the energy forms listed in the competency, so it is unrelated to the intended subject.

copy.en: Some tiny microalgae can store lots of oil in their cells — scientists are studying algae as a renewable biofuel to replace fossil fuels!
copy.tl: Ang ilang microalgae ay nag-iimbak ng malaking halaga ng langis sa kanilang mga cell — pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang algae bilang renewable na biofuel na maaaring pumalit sa fossil fuels!
copy.bis: Ang uban nga microalgae makatipig og daghang lana sa ilang mga cell — gitun-an sa mga siyentipiko ang algae isip renewable nga biofuel nga mahimong makapuli sa fossil fuels!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: help plants grow and improve the soil
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses algae/seaweed as fertilizer providing nutrients and improving soil, but does not address observing outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their roles in obtaining water and nutrients. It shares the topic of plant nutrition but does not directly support the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: improve the soil
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in a guided investigation to identify the effect of different types of soil on the growth of plants
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions improving soil and helping plants grow, but it does not describe an investigation into the effect of different types of soil on plant growth. It is about fertilizer addition, not comparing soil types, so it does not directly support the guided investigation competency.

copy.en: Algae and seaweed are used as organic fertilizer in farming — they're rich in nitrogen, phosphorus, and other minerals that help plants grow and improve the soil.
copy.tl: Ang algae at seaweed ay ginagamit bilang organic na abono sa pagsasaka — mayaman ang mga ito sa nitrogen, phosphorus, at iba pang mineral na tumutulong sa paglaki ng halaman at nagpapabuti sa lupa.
copy.bis: Ang algae ug seaweed gigamit ingon organic nga abono sa pagpanguma — dato sila sa nitrogen, phosphorus, ug uban pang mineral nga nagtabang sa pagtubo sa tanom ug nagpaayo sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whether complete or incomplete, insect metamorphosis always starts the same way — hatching from an egg.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about the first stage of insect metamorphosis. It does not use a flow chart, does not compare different stages, and does not address the life cycles of the named animals (butterfly, frog, chicken, human). The content is only topically related to life cycles.

copy.en: Whether complete or incomplete, insect metamorphosis always starts the same way — hatching from an egg.
copy.tl: Kompleto man o hindi, palaging sa pagpisa mula sa itlog nagsisimula ang metamorphosis ng insekto.
copy.bis: Kompleto man o dili, kanunay sa pagbutho gikan sa itlog nagsugod ang metamorphosis sa insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An allergy happens when your immune system overreacts to something harmless
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the immune system's overreaction, but G4-L-1 specifically lists muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The immune system is not among them, so the card does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An allergy happens when your immune system overreacts to something harmless
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: G8-L-2 requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The card is a simple statement about allergies and does not use any required representation nor explain how body systems work together. It only mentions the immune system reacting, which is not the focus of the competency.

copy.en: An allergy happens when your immune system overreacts to something harmless — like dust or pollen — treating it like a dangerous invader.
copy.tl: Nangyayari ang allergy kapag sobrang lumalaban ang immune system sa isang bagay na hindi naman mapanganib, gaya ng alikabok o pollen.
copy.bis: Mahitabo ang alerdyi kon sobra nga makig-away ang immune system sa butang nga dili diay peligroso, sama sa abog o pollen.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An alloy is a cool material made by mixing two or more metals together, or mixing a metal with another element!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an alloy as a mixture of metals, but G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. The card does not classify alloys as uniform or non-uniform, nor does it provide the required examples or contrast.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An alloy is a cool material made by mixing two or more metals together, or mixing a metal with another element!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain properties of metals in terms of their structure and metallic bonding (sea of electrons model)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions metals and mixing, but G9-M-10 requires explaining properties of metals in terms of their structure and metallic bonding (sea of electrons model). The card provides no information about metallic bonding, structure, or properties, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: An alloy is a cool material made by mixing two or more metals together, or mixing a metal with another element!
copy.tl: Ang aleasyon ay isang napakagandang materyal na gawa sa paghahalo ng dalawa o higit pang metal, o metal at ibang sangkap!
copy.bis: Ang aleasyon usa ka nindot nga materyal nga gihimo pinaagi sa pagsagol sa duha o sobra pa nga metal, o metal ug laing elemento!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Above it, the cold and wind are too harsh, so only moss and grasses survive.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions harsh cold and wind and that only moss and grasses survive, but it does not explain how plants are adapted to these unfavorable conditions. It only states a fact about the treeline, not the mechanism of adaptation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Above it, the cold and wind are too harsh, so only moss and grasses survive.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cold and wind as environmental factors and living things (moss, grasses), but it does not describe them as biotic or abiotic factors in an ecosystem. It does not teach the concept of biotic vs. abiotic factors.

copy.en:
Why are there no trees on very high mountains?

There's a line called the treeline — the highest spot trees can grow. Above it, the cold and wind are too harsh, so only moss and grasses survive.
copy.tl:
Bakit walang puno sa napakataas na bahagi ng bundok?

May tinatawag na treeline — ang pinakamataas na altitude kung saan pwedeng lumaki ang puno. Sa itaas nito, sobrang tindi ng lamig at hangin, kaya lumot at damo na lang ang nabubuhay.
copy.bis:
Nganong walay kahoy sa taas kaayo nga bahin sa bukid?

Naa'y gitawag nga treeline — ang pinakataas nga altitude diin makatubo ang kahoy. Sa ibabaw niini, hilabihan ka grabe ang katugnaw ug hangin, mao nga lumot ug balili na lang ang mabuhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sinks because its density (2.7 g/cm³) is higher than water's!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains sinking using density, not the listed factors (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture) as movement-affecting properties. It mentions 'too heavy for its size' but frames it as density, so it does not directly teach the competency's exploration of factors affecting object movement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sinks because its density (2.7 g/cm³) is higher than water's!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and floating/sinking, not the definition of matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It does not directly support identifying matter by mass and volume.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sinks because its density (2.7 g/cm³) is higher than water's!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses density to explain sinking but does not describe the Particle Model of Matter, particles, or that each pure substance has its own kind of particles. It is only tangentially related to matter concepts.

copy.en:
Why does aluminum sink in water?

It sinks because its density (2.7 g/cm³) is higher than water's! It's just too heavy for its size to float.
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulubog ang aluminyo (aluminum) sa tubig?

Lumulubog ito dahil mas mataas ang densidad nito (2.7 g/cm³) kaysa tubig! Masyado itong siksik para lumutang.
copy.bis:
Nganong molunod ang aluminum (aluminyo) sa tubig?

Molunod kini kay mas taas ang density niini (2.7 g/cm³) kaysa tubig! Gisiksik kaayo kini mao nga dili makalutaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all amethysts are the same shade! Some are pale lavender, while others are deep purple.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes color variation in amethyst, a rock, but does not involve exploring, observing, or collecting rocks in the school grounds or local area, nor does it compare multiple rock types across features like texture or grain crystal size. It only provides a fact about one mineral's color, which is related vocabulary but not direct instructional support for the competency's activity.

copy.en: Not all amethysts are the same shade! Some are pale lavender, while others are deep purple. This depends on the iron and radiation they received.
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng amethyst ay pareho ng kulay! May maputlang lavender, at may napakadilim na purple. Nakadepende ito sa iron at radiation na natanggap nito.
copy.bis: Dili tanan amethyst parehas og kolor! Adunay luspad nga lavender, ug adunay lawom kaayo nga purple. Nagdepende kini sa puthaw ug radiation nga nadawat niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It takes thousands of years for large crystals to form as mineral-rich water slowly adds quartz layer by layer.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses amethyst crystal formation over time, but the competency requires exploring/collecting rocks and comparing features like texture, color, and grain crystal size. No such observation or comparison is present.

copy.en: Amethyst doesn't grow fast! It takes thousands of years for large crystals to form as mineral-rich water slowly adds quartz layer by layer.
copy.tl: Hindi mabilis lumaki ang amethyst! Tumatagal ng libo-libong taon para mabuo ang malalaking kristal habang dahan-dahang nagdadagdag ng quartz ang tubig.
copy.bis: Dili paspas motubo ang amethyst! Mokabat og liboan ka tuig aron maporma ang dagkong kristal samtang hinay-hinay nga magdugang og quartz ang tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ampalaya, or bitter gourd, is a bumpy-skinned vine vegetable known for its bitter taste
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ampalaya as a vegetable and mentions its taste and a health belief, but it does not describe any outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their roles in obtaining water and nutrients. It shares only the broad subject of plants.

copy.en:
What is ampalaya?

Ampalaya, or bitter gourd, is a bumpy-skinned vine vegetable known for its bitter taste — many eat it because it's believed to help control blood sugar.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ampalaya?

Ang ampalaya ay isang gulay na baging na may kulubot na balat at kilalang mapait ang lasa — madalas itong kainin dahil sinasabing nakakatulong ito sa pagkontrol ng asukal sa dugo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang ampalaya?

Ang ampalaya usa ka utanon nga nagakatay nga may kulubot nga panit ug ilado nga pait — kanunay kini kan-on kay giingong makatabang sa pagkontrol sa asukal sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It was named after the scientist Andre-Marie Ampere.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a famous foreign scientist (Andre-Marie Ampere) and a unit named after him, but the competency specifically asks for the scientist's invention/s. The ampere is a unit of measurement, not an invention, so the card does not directly support identifying an invention.

copy.en:
What do we call the unit of electric current?

It is the ampere, or amp for short! It was named after the scientist Andre-Marie Ampere.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa yunit ng electric current?

Ito ay ang ampere, o amp! Ipinangalan ito sa dakilang siyentipikong si Andre-Marie Ampere.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa yunit sa electric current?

Mao kini ang ampere, o amp! Ginganlan kini sa dakong siyentipiko nga si Andre-Marie Ampere.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is the beautiful Andromeda!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Andromeda as the nearest large galaxy, but it does not involve guided observation or description of commonly seen daytime/nighttime sky objects such as the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. Andromeda is not presented as a commonly observed celestial object, so it only shares the broad sky/space topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is the beautiful Andromeda!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: G5-E-11 is about the general structure of the solar system and its major celestial objects. Andromeda is a separate galaxy outside the solar system, so the card does not support describing the solar system's structure, names, features, or composition.

copy.en:
What is the nearest large galaxy to our Milky Way?

The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is the beautiful Andromeda!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalapit na malaking galaksiya sa Milky Way natin?

Ang pinakamalapit na malaking galaksiya sa Milky Way ay ang Andromeda!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang labing duol nga dako nga galaksiya sa atong Milky Way?

Ang labing duol nga dako nga galaksiya sa Milky Way mao ang Andromeda!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Surgery changed forever in 1846, the year ether anesthesia was first shown to the public.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a historical science event (ether anesthesia demonstration) but does not identify any scientist or their invention, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Surgery changed forever in 1846, the year ether anesthesia was first shown to the public.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use information from home or local community, nor does it explain the impact of a science invention on everyday life. It only states a historical fact about ether anesthesia.

copy.en: Surgery changed forever in 1846, the year ether anesthesia was first shown to the public.
copy.tl: Nagbago ang operasyon noong taong 1846, nang unang ipinakita sa publiko ang ether anesthesia.
copy.bis: Nausab ang operasyon niadtong tuig 1846, dihang unang gipakita sa publiko ang ether anesthesia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Only the deep-sea ones glow — shallow-water kinds use their rod as a lure with no light at all.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a difference between deep-sea and shallow-water anglerfish species, but does not explain how any animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or adaptation. It only notes that some species glow and others do not.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 'Anglerfish' is a huge group of many species.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that anglerfish is a group of many species, but it does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, fungi, bacteria). It provides no classification information and does not meet the format requirement of a table.

copy.en:
Do all anglerfish glow in the dark?

No! 'Anglerfish' is a huge group of many species. Only the deep-sea ones glow — shallow-water kinds use their rod as a lure with no light at all.
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng anglerfish ay nagliliwanag?

Hindi pala! Ang 'anglerfish' ay malaking grupo ng maraming uri. Yung nasa malalim na dagat lang ang may liwanag — yung nasa mababaw na tubig ay gumagamit ng pamingwit na walang ilaw.
copy.bis:
Tanan ba nga anglerfish nagsiga?

Dili diay! Ang 'anglerfish' usa ka dako nga grupo sa daghang klase. Ang naa sa lawom nga dagat ra ang nagsiga — ang naa sa mabaw nga tubig mogamit sa pamingwit nga walay siga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many animals find their way on long journeys using smell, the sun and stars, Earth's magnetic field, and memory

No! Animals like dogs, cats, and carabaos pee too, to get rid of waste from their bodies!

Hindi lang tao ang umiihi! Ang mga hayop tulad ng aso, pusa, at kalabaw ay umiihi rin para maialis ang dumi sa katawan!
copy.bis:
Tawo ra ba ang mangihi?

Dili lang tawo ang mangihi! Ang mga mananap sama sa iro, iring, ug kalabaw mangihi usab aron makuha ang hugaw sa ilang lawas!

copy.bis: Daghan sa mga hulmigas manalipod sa ilang kaugalingon pinaagi sa pagpaak, ug ang uban adunay tusok o asido nga makapaso aron abugon ang kaaway!

What do ants eat?

Ants eat many different things — sweet food, crumbs, seeds, and even small dead insects they find.
copy.tl:
Ano ang kinakain ng langgam?

Ang mga langgam ay kumakain ng iba't ibang bagay — matatamis na pagkain, mumo, buto, at maliliit na patay na insekto na nakikita nila.
copy.bis:
Unsay kaonon sa hulmigas?

Ang mga hulmigas mokaon og lainlaing butang — tam-is nga pagkaon, mumho, liso, ug gagmayng patay nga insekto nga ilang makit-an.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions eggs but does not identify which animal groups give birth to live young versus lay eggs, nor does it classify ants as egg-layers. It only describes colony decline after queen death, which does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without a new queen, no new eggs appear.

assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on reproduction indirectly (eggs are needed for colony survival) but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It focuses on colony fate, not on the general characteristics of living things.

copy.en:
What happens when an ant queen dies?

Without a new queen, no new eggs appear. Slowly the colony fades until the last workers die and the whole nest disappears.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kapag namatay ang reyna ng langgam?

Kapag walang bagong reyna, wala nang bagong itlog. Unti-unti nang mauubos ang kolonya hanggang mamatay ang mga huling manggagawa at mawala ang buong pugad.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung mamatay ang reyna sa hulmigas?

Kung walay bag-ong reyna, wala nay bag-ong itlog. Hinay-hinay nga mahurot ang kolonya hangtod mamatay ang kataposang mga trabahante ug mahanaw ang tibuok salag.

copy.en:
Do male ants guard the queen?

Many think a 'king' ant guards the queen, but male ants only exist to mate during the flight — after that, they die quickly and never work or guard the nest.
copy.tl:
Nagbabantay ba ang lalaking langgam sa reyna?

Marami ang nag-aakalang may 'hari' na nagbabantay sa reyna, pero ang mga lalaking langgam ay para lang makipagtalik sa paglipad — pagkatapos, mabilis silang mamamatay at hindi na nagtatrabaho o nagbabantay sa pugad.
copy.bis:
Nagbantay ba ang laki nga hulmigas sa reyna?

Daghan ang naghunahuna nga adunay 'hari' nga nagbantay sa reyna, apan ang mga lalaki nga hulmigas para ra makigminyo sa paglupad — human niana, paspas silang mamatay ug dili na motrabaho o mobantay sa salag.

copy.en: A young winged female ant that hasn't mated yet is called an 'alate,' or virgin queen. She becomes a true queen only after flying, mating, and laying eggs.
copy.tl: Ang batang babaeng langgam na may pakpak pero hindi pa nakikipagtalik ay tinatawag na 'alate' o virgin queen. Magiging tunay na reyna lang siya pagkatapos lumipad, makipagtalik, at mangitlog.
copy.bis: Ang batan-ong babaye nga hulmigas nga may pako apan wala pa makighilawas gitawag og 'alate' o virgin queen. Mahimo lang siyang tinuod nga reyna human makalupad, makigminyo, ug mangitlog.

Which animal is the strongest for its size?

The ant is one of the strongest animals alive — it can carry objects many times heavier than its own body!
copy.tl:
Aling hayop ang pinakamalakas sa laki nito?

Isa ang langgam sa pinakamalakas na hayop — kaya nitong buhatin ang bagay na mas mabigat ng maraming beses kaysa sarili nitong timbang!
copy.bis:
Unsang hayop ang pinakakusgan sa iyang gidak-on?

Usa ang hulmigas sa pinakakusgan nga hayop — makahimo kini modala og butang nga mas bug-at og daghang pilo sa iyang gibug-aton!

copy.tl: Kapag laganap na ang resistensya, nagiging mahirap gamutin at mas mapanganib ang mga karaniwang impeksyong dating madaling lunasan.
copy.bis: Kung mokaylap na ang resistensya, mahimong lisod tambalan ug mas delikado ang mga komon nga impeksiyon nga kaniadto sayon ra ayohon.

copy.en:
Do antibiotics relieve pain or fever?

No — antibiotics are not painkillers and don't lower fever. They're only used when there's a bacterial infection.
copy.tl:
Nakababawas ba ng sakit o lagnat ang antibiotic?

Hindi — hindi pamatay-sakit ang antibiotic at hindi ito nagpapababa ng lagnat. Ginagamit lang ito kapag may impeksyong dulot ng bakterya.
copy.bis:
Makapaminusan ba og sakit o hilanat ang antibyotiko?

Dili — dili pamatay-sakit ang antibyotiko ug dili kini makapaubos og hilanat. Gigamit ra kini kung naay impeksiyon nga gikan sa bakterya.

An ant can carry things that are heavier than its own body!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabigat ang kayang buhatin ng langgam?

Kayang bitbitin ng isang langgam ang bagay na mas mabigat pa sa sarili nitong katawan!
copy.bis:
Pila ka bug-at ang madala sa hulmigas?

Ang usa ka hulmigas makahimo og pas-an sa butang nga mas bug-at pa sa iyang lawas!

copy.tl: Pinoprotektahan ng mga siyentista at gobyerno ang mga apex predator gaya ng pating at agila dahil alam nilang kung mawawala ang mga ito, magugulo ang balanse ng dagat o gubat na pinagkukunan din ng pagkain at hanapbuhay ng tao.
copy.bis: Gipanalipdan sa mga syentista ug gobyerno ang mga apex predator sama sa iho ug agila kay nahibalo sila nga kon mawala kini, magubot ang timbang sa dagat o lasang nga gigikanan usab sa pagkaon ug panginabuhi sa tawo.

assignedReviews.reason: Top hunters are not trophic levels as levels of energy in a food pyramid.

copy.en:
What makes tigers apex predators?

On land, big cats like tigers and lions are apex predators — the top hunters in their habitat. No other animal regularly dares to eat a healthy, full-grown one!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapa-apex predator sa tigre?

Sa lupa, ang malalaking pusa tulad ng tigre at leon ay apex predator — ang pinakamatatapang na manghuhuli sa kanilang tirahan. Walang ibang hayop ang regular na nangahas kumain sa kanila kapag malusog at malaki na sila!
copy.bis:
Unsay hinungdan nga apex predator ang tigre?

Sa yuta, ang dagkong iring sama sa tigre ug leon mao ang apex predator — ang pinakaisog nga mangangayam sa ilang puy-anan. Walay laing hayop nga kanunay mangahas mokaon kanila kon himsog ug dako na sila!

copy.bis: Ang mga aphid gagmayng insekto nga nagsupsup sa katas sa tanom — paspas sila mudaghan ug makadaot og dako sa mga tanom ug hardin.

What giant rocket sent Apollo 11 to the Moon?

Apollo 11 was sent to the Moon by the giant Saturn V rocket in 1969!
copy.tl:
Anong higanteng rocket ang nagdala sa Apollo 11 papuntang buwan?

Ang Apollo 11 ay dinala sa buwan ng higanteng rocket na Saturn V noong 1969!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang higanteng rocket nga nagdala sa Apollo 11 paingon sa bulan?

Ang Apollo 11 gidala sa bulan sa higanteng rocket nga Saturn V niadtong 1969!

copy.bis: Ang apendiks usa ka gamayng organ nga makita sa ubos nga tuong bahin sa imong tiyan.

copy.bis: Ang aquamarine beryl usab, parehas sa emerald, apan asul o asul-berde ang kolor!

copy.en:
Why do objects float in water?

According to Archimedes' principle, the upward buoyant force on an object equals the weight of the water it displaces. That is exactly why things float!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang mga bagay sa tubig?

Ayon sa Archimedes' principle, ang pataas na buoyant force sa isang bagay ay katumbas ng timbang ng tubig na pinalabas nito. Kaya nga lumulutang ang mga bagay!
copy.bis:
Nganong mulutaw ang mga butang sa tubig?

Sumala sa Archimedes' principle, ang pataas nga buoyant force sa butang katumbas sa timbang sa tubig nga iyang gibalhin. Mao ni ang hinungdan ngano mulutaw ang mga butang!
